question: If your nose is blocked, the olfactory receptors are NOT able to detect:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Olfactory receptors are responsible for the sense of smell.
 
• When the nose is blocked, the passage of air to the olfactory receptors is obstructed.
 
• This obstruction prevents the olfactory receptors from detecting odor molecules effectively.
 
• Smell is directly linked to the function of olfactory receptors, which are located in the nasal cavity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Olfactory System:**

 
 
• The olfactory system is the sensory system used for smelling (olfaction).
 
• It includes the olfactory receptors, olfactory bulb, and various brain regions involved in processing smell.
 
 
 
• **Olfactory Receptors:**
 
 
• These are specialized sensory cells located in the nasal cavity.
 
• They detect odor molecules and send signals to the brain.
 
 
 
• **Function of Smell:**
 
 
• Smell is vital for detecting dangers, such as smoke or spoiled food.
 
• It also plays a role in taste perception and memory recall.
 
 
 
• **Blockage of the Nose:**
 
 
• Nasal blockage can be caused by colds, allergies, or sinus infections.
 
• This blockage hinders the ability to smell by preventing odor molecules from reaching the olfactory receptors.
